drivingQuestion: Why is one who covered the blood and saw it uncovered exempt from covering it again, when the obligation to return a lost item applies even a hundred times?
outcomeNote: The question is left standing here; Rav Ashi's answer follows in the next unit.

segments.he: כִּסָּהוּ וְנִתְגַּלָּה. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: מַאי שְׁנָא מֵהֲשָׁבַת אֲבֵדָה, דְּאָמַר מָר: ״הָשֵׁב״ – אֲפִילּוּ מֵאָה פְּעָמִים.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that if one «covered» the blood «and it was» then «uncovered» he is not obligated to cover it again. «Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi: What is different» about this case from the mitzva of «returning a lost item, where the Master said:» The verse states with regard to the obligation to return a lost item: «“You shall return» them to your brother” (Deuteronomy 22:1), «even one hundred times?»

moves.summary: The gemara quotes the mishna's clause that blood covered and then uncovered need not be covered again.
moves.about: quoting the mishna's clause that if one covered the blood and it became uncovered he need not cover it again

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב אחא בריה דרבא לרב אשי: מאי שנא
moves.summary: Rav Aha asks Rav Ashi why this differs from returning a lost item.
moves.about: why covering that came undone need not be repeated, when returning a lost item must be repeated even a hundred times

moves.summary: He cites the Master's rule that you shall return them means even one hundred times.
moves.about: citing the doubled verb of you shall surely return them as requiring restoration even a hundred times
